per_shot.note: Gallery doorway reads as a lit, signed portal at the hall's east end; the wing beyond is only a dim magenta wash and the hall floor is dark with blotchy, smeared reflections.

Reads as a museum: overhead spot cones, glass cases, placards, a coloured pool under each plinth, and colour washing up onto the ceiling. The mirror-like floor streaks make it look wet, and the plinth bodies are black stumps.

Tank colours (amber/ice/green/violet) wash the ceiling and floor, so the room feels lit by its tanks. The creatures read as flat, pale holograms more than living light, and the floor streaks are again too glossy.

top_issues.issue: The floor is a near-perfect mirror with long vertical colour streaks
top_issues.why: It reads as wet glass, not hab plating. It competes with the exhibits and takes up the bottom 40% of the frame with streaks instead of pools.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise floor roughness so each source lands as a soft, short pool under its plinth or tank. Keep a faint sheen, and keep the plate seams visible.

top_issues.issue: Plinths and tank bases are featureless black masses
top_issues.why: In a museum the pedestal is part of the display. Here the spot light stops at the case, so the stones float over dark stumps.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the plinths a lighter stone or metal top with a lit bevel, and let the spot cone carry down onto the plinth face and placard.

top_issues.issue: The vivarium creatures are pale, low-contrast silhouettes
top_issues.why: 'Creatures remembered as light' should glow from within. Right now the tank tint carries the light and the creatures look like translucent cutouts, with little bloom of their own.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise each creature's emissive above its tank tint and give it a soft core bloom, so the creature is the brightest thing in its tank and the tank colour comes from it.

top_issues.issue: The exhibit walls behind the cases are under-dressed
top_issues.why: Between the cases the walls are a dim, uniform band, so the wings feel like a row of props against a corridor more than a designed room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add small wall-washes or a picture rail and nameplate band behind each case, so every bay is its own lit alcove.

top_issues.issue: The wing is barely visible from the hall
top_issues.why: The showpiece wing should invite you in, but from the hall it shows only a dark magenta haze past the doorway.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let one exhibit's glow spill through the doorway onto the hall floor near the GALLERY sign.

protect: Overhead spot cones and coloured light pools under each exhibit
Per-tank colour identity (amber/ice/green/violet) and the coloured tank rims
Coloured washes on the ceiling, so the ceiling is never a black slab
The suit stays the most legible thing in every frame
Warm porthole dusk between the gallery cases

per_shot.note: Essentially the same hall. The floor is a little warmer and brighter with better pools, but there is an odd red band along the bottom edge. The wing beyond the door is still just dim haze.
The stones bloom more strongly inside their cases (gold, ruby and diamond glow). The floor pools are softer and less wet. But the ceiling drops toward black, and the big halos blur the case edges.
The softer floor is an improvement, but the upper third falls nearly to black. The tank light no longer washes the ceiling, so the room reads darker and less lit by its tanks.

top_issues.issue: The ceiling falls back toward a black slab
top_issues.why: The direction explicitly rejects a black ceiling, and the wings should be 'lit by living light that lands on the room'. A shows the tank and stone colour reaching the ceiling; B loses most of it.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Restore the coloured bounce on the ceiling panels and beams from A, while keeping B's softer floor.

top_issues.issue: Stone bloom halos are wide and wash out the glass cases
top_issues.why: The glow is lovely, but the halo swallows the case frames, so the 'glass vitrine' read weakens.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tighten the bloom radius a little, or lower its intensity, so the case edges stay crisp around a glowing stone.

top_issues.issue: Plinths and tank bases are featureless black masses
top_issues.why: The pedestal is part of the display, and the stones and creatures float over dark stumps.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Light the plinth tops and faces and carry the spot cone down onto the placard.

top_issues.issue: The vivarium creatures are pale silhouettes with little light of their own
top_issues.why: In the darker B frame the creatures should carry the light, and they do not.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise the creatures' emissive and core bloom above the tank tint.

top_issues.issue: Red band along the bottom edge of the hall frame
top_issues.why: It reads as an artefact or foreground trim that serves no purpose and pulls the eye.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop it, or darken it into the floor edge.

protect: Softer, diffused floor reflections (less wet-glass than A)
Strong in-case stone bloom, so the stones read as glowing gems
Placards, spot cones and per-tank colour identity
The suit stays the most legible thing in the frame

why: In A the exhibit light reaches the ceiling and the room, so the wings feel lit by their showpieces. B's softer floor and stronger gem bloom are real gains, but B lets the upper third fall to near-black. Best would be A's room light combined with B's floor and bloom.
